chunks: He said: Al-Sharif Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Tahir al-Musavi reported to us from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed al-Hamdani, who reported from Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban, who reported from Muhammad ibn Sinan, who reported from Ahmad ibn Sulayman al-Qummi al-Kufi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, saying:

Even a prophet among the prophets would be tested with hunger until he died of it; and even a prophet among the prophets would be tested with thirst until he died of it; and even a prophet among the prophets would be tested with exposure until he died naked; and even a prophet among the prophets would be tested with illness and diseases until they consumed him; and even a prophet among the prophets would come to his people and stand among them, commanding them to obey Allah and calling them to the unity of Allah, yet he would not even have lodging for a single night. They would not let him complete his speech, nor would they listen to him, until they killed him. Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, tests His servants according to their stations in His estimation.
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah test His prophets and servants with suffering according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) describes the severe trials endured by prophets throughout history. He enumerates specific forms of suffering — hunger, thirst, exposure, illness, and martyrdom — emphasizing that some prophets died from these afflictions, and that some were killed by their own people while calling them to God's unity. The teaching was directed at his close companions to help them understand that divine testing is proportional to one's spiritual rank, and that suffering is not a sign of God's displeasure but rather a mark of elevated status.
